newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rain said urgently needed in south NSW Australia.
newsitem.headline: Rain said urgently needed in south NSW Australia.

text.p: A lack of any significant rainfall over much of the southern half of the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) had resulted in an increase in the area of the state drought-declared, state Agriculture Minister Richard Amery said on Wednesday.
The area of the state drought-declared for April was 27 percent, up from 19 percent in March, he said in a statement.
In southern areas, autumn was traditionally dry with producers looking for a rain break in April to promote winter forage species and to enable winter crop preparation.
Despite good falls in the first few days of March, the Monaro region missed out on follow-up rainfall and agricultural response had been burnt off with continued warm dry winds, he said.
The Monaro and parts of the central and southern tablelands now required good soaking rains as a matter of urgency to avoid a severe winter, he said.
Sheep and cattle comprise the main farm enterprises in these areas.
